name: ssd-bench-qa-sqlite-internals
notes: Long-form Q&A: deep SQLite internals questions with multi-part answers expected. ~630 prompt tokens.

messages.content:
I am building a production Rust service that uses SQLite (via rusqlite) as an embedded metrics and index store. The database is written to by a single background thread (WAL mode, PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL) and read by up to 12 concurrent async worker threads. I have the following technical questions:

Question 1: WAL checkpointing.
SQLite WAL mode uses a write-ahead log that accumulates writes until a checkpoint copies them into the main database file. What triggers a checkpoint? What is the difference between a PASSIVE, FULL, RESTART, and TRUNCATE checkpoint? In my setup, the background writer thread calls PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=1000 (checkpoint every 1000 pages). Is there a risk that concurrent readers will block a checkpoint from completing? How do I detect and handle a stuck WAL that grows without bound?

Question 2: Page cache and memory usage.
SQLite has a per-connection page cache (PRAGMA cache_size). In my setup, 12 reader connections each have PRAGMA cache_size=4000 (4000 pages × 4 KB = 16 MB per connection = 192 MB total). I want to reduce memory usage. Is there a way to share a page cache across connections in the same process? What is the shared-cache mode and why does SQLite documentation warn against it for WAL mode? What is the actual memory impact of enabling shared-cache with WAL — will it cause correctness issues?

Question 3: Index design for time-range queries.
My events table has ~5 million rows after 30 days of production traffic. It has columns: id INTEGER PK, run_id TEXT, ts_utc TEXT, op TEXT, value REAL, notes TEXT. My most common query is: SELECT AVG(value) FROM events WHERE op = 'ssd_spill' AND ts_utc BETWEEN '2026-05-14T00:00:00Z' AND '2026-05-14T23:59:59Z'. I have a single-column index on op and a single-column index on ts_utc. Will SQLite use both indexes for this query via an index merge? How can I verify which index plan is chosen? Would a composite index on (op, ts_utc) be better? What is the rule for column order in composite indexes for range predicates?

Question 4: VACUUM and page reuse.
My index.db (the SSD KV-cache block index) has high insert-and-delete churn: I insert a new row per spilled block and delete rows during LRU eviction. After running for a week with 50,000 evictions, the database is 800 MB but PRAGMA page_count * page_size shows only 120 MB of live data. The other 680 MB is free pages. How does SQLite reuse free pages? Under what conditions does the file shrink without a VACUUM? Should I run VACUUM INTO periodically or PRAGMA auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL? What is the performance cost of incremental auto-vacuum on my insert-heavy workload?

Question 5: rusqlite connection pooling.
In my Rust code, I wrap each rusqlite::Connection in a Mutex<Connection>. For the 12 reader threads, I have a pool of 4 connections in a Vec<Mutex<Connection>> and each reader picks the first non-blocked one via try_lock(). Is this the standard pattern? Are there correctness issues with having multiple connections open on the same WAL-mode SQLite file from the same process? Is there a deadlock scenario if two connections both try to start a write transaction simultaneously in WAL mode?
